sessions.lever: Group C closed (no-arg call); phantom-slot PRODUCER identified via combine orphan-USE RTL
sessions.note: GROUP C CLOSED 48->47: func_8007DC9C() takes NO argument. The committed source passed (u32 *)0xA0000000, emitting `lui a0,0xa000` where target has a nop at idx 66 - exactly what the rule `subst "lui\s+\$4,..." "nop" @ 63` papered over. func_8007DC9C(0) and (u32 *)0 both stay at 48, so it must be no argument at all rather than a null one. GROUP A PRODUCER IDENTIFIED EXACTLY: each phantom frame slot is one combine orphan-USE pseudo, and the producer is an s16->s32 sign-extension of a value ALREADY IN A REGISTER. GCC expands it as (set (reg:SI 96) (ashift:SI (subreg:SI (reg/v:HI 75) 0) 16)) + (set (reg:SI 95) (ashiftrt:SI (reg:SI 96) 16)); combine merges the pair into one sign_extend, killing 96's def but leaving (use (reg:SI 96)) orphaned, and greg reports it UNALLOCATED so it takes an 8-byte slot. tmp/orphan_probe.py on our body reports UNALLOCATED ['96','100'] - exactly two strands, exactly vars=16. A value loaded straight from memory does NOT count because lh sign-extends in the load. So the Group A spec is: go from 2 orphan strands to 4. NEGATIVE: extra s16 casts do NOT create strands - six spellings (s16 xf=arg0->x with (s32)xf, s16 yf=(s16)(v0_ext>>16) with (s32)yf, both, the clamped x as s16 xc, both clamp limits as s16 with explicit (s32) widening) ALL still report exactly 2 unallocated pseudos and vars=16, because re-casting an already-s16 value is a no-op GCC folds; three of them also collapsed the multiply to 131 insns. src/display.c reverted; candidate.c carries the Group-C fix plus the cheat-asm removal.

sessions.lever: the named real-s16-quantity family (clamp-limit carriers, clamped-dimension locals, natural w/h idiom)
sessions.note: THE NAMED FAMILY DOES NOT DELIVER GROUP A, but the round produced the single most useful fact so far. Six variants, every local REAL (holding a value the body already computes and uses): the two clamp limits as s16 locals used by both the compare and the clamping assignment; the same hoisted to the top of the body; the clamped height as an s16 local feeding both the store and the shift; the natural w/h dimension-local clamp idiom with control flow preserved; and three combinations. All but one hold at exactly 2 orphans / 142 insns / score 47. THE EXCEPTION IS THE HANDLE: `lim_top` (both clamp globals read once into s16 xlim/ylim at the top, used by both compares) gives orphans=1, vars=8, frame=56 AT THE SAME 142 INSTRUCTIONS (score 55), reproduced. That refutes any 'vars is stuck at 16' reading - the strand count DOES move with source shape, just downward so far. Mechanistically, hoisting the load away from its compare REMOVED a strand, so a strand requires the widening to sit where combine cannot fold it into the load; the next session should work that lever in reverse. TWO HARD CONSTRAINTS on any candidate, both derived from target: the multiply must keep RE-READING arg0->x from memory (target splice regfix.txt:3417 is `lh $3,4($17)` ... `mult $3,$2`), and target emits the same two `sll ,0x10` + one `sra ,0x10` we do, so the two extra strands must be widenings combine folds away entirely. DISCIPLINE: no synthetic-strand spelling was tried and none should be - nothing reaches 3 or 4 orphans by any means, real or not, so there is no 'only works with a semantically empty local' trade-off to adjudicate. Banked on measurement, not on a policy call. src/display.c reverted.

(A) The frame is 16 bytes short because cc1 allocates half as many phantom locals temps as the original did (vars 16 vs 32) - not a spill, not a dead array, and not reachable by declaring locals. (B) Register allocation in the clamp and multiply blocks plus three extra/missing moves. (C) One superfluous argument load at the func_8007DC9C call.
